narrative.northStar: The Lamplit Desk Beside the City
narrative.overview:
AWS City is two things side by side: a bright, generated pixel-art city (one per AWS Region, drawn on a 32×16 isometric grid) and a quiet warm-graphite desk where the player reads, decides and approves. The desk exists to let the city carry the colour. Its surfaces are near-black graphite with a warm cast, its text is parchment-white rather than pure white, and a single amber lamp (the accent) marks the one thing to do next. Paper (cream flashcards, white speech bubbles, the gold of a found token) appears only where the city "speaks" into the desk.

Density is high but small: 13 px body text, 8 px and 12 px gaps, 6 px corners, everything sized to work first in a 400 px browser side panel and then reused unchanged as the right-hand column of the full tab. Motion is short and stepped like sprite frames, and a big moment in the city plays in order, one thing at a time. Every visual setting a player can change (text size, contrast, font, motion) is a token override, never a second stylesheet.
keyCharacteristics: Warm graphite surfaces layered by tone (bg → panel → panel-2 → panel-hi), with hairline borders instead of shadows.
One amber primary per screen; district colours only as small identity marks.
Nunito for everything readable; Press Start 2P only for the wordmark and a few game labels, on its 8 px grid.
The pixel city is the only hard-edged, saturated thing on screen; the UI recedes around it.
The side panel (400 px) is the design's first surface; the tab adds a wide stage, not a different UI.
The canvas wears the same tokens: the mini-games' chrome is the desk's graphite and amber, and its text follows Text size.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: One amber-filled button per screen (the smoke test counts them on the City tab). Everything else is a quiet graphite button, a ghost or a chip.

rules.name: The District Square Rule
rules.body: A district's colour appears as a small mark (an 8 px square, a 4 px progress segment, an eyebrow word), never as a background.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Colours come from :root in src/app/styles/00-base.css (and src/game/theme.ts mirrors them for Phaser under the same names). Accessibility modes work by overriding these tokens, so a raw hex in a component escapes them.

rules.name: The 12 px Floor Rule
rules.body: 12 px is the floor for body text; 11 px only for non-essential labels. No shipped exceptions: tab badges are 11 px and the wordmark is --fs-pixel.

rules.name: The 11 px Canvas Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing a player reads on the canvas is under 11 px, at any text size or zoom. A line too long for its place shrinks to the floor, then wraps (the Red Team Range's log lines); it never shrinks further.

rules.name: The Pixel Grid Rule
rules.body: Press Start 2P only at its two tokens, --fs-pixel 11 px and --fs-pixel-lg 15 px (15 and 19 px at the bigger text sizes). Never scale it by a fraction.

rules.name: The Heavy-Weight Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is weight (700/800), not colour or italics; most labels and buttons are 700–800.

rules.name: The Whole Pixel Rule
rules.body: Pixel art moves and scales on whole pixels: integer zoom at rest, whole-number sprite scales, positions rounded, confetti turning in quarter turns. A fractional zoom is allowed only mid-tween.

rules.name: The Flat Desk Rule
rules.body: Cards in the side column are flat (tone and hairline). Only what floats over the city (menus, toasts, sheets, the coin note) gets the float shadow.

dos: Do take every colour, size, gap and radius from the tokens in 00-base.css (and theme.ts for the canvas), so the text-size, high-contrast and easy-read modes in 22-access.css reach it.
Do keep one amber primary per screen and say exactly what it does ("Review 5 cards", "Walk to S3 Lake").
Do design for the 400 px side panel first, then check the 1400 × 880 tab.
Do keep district colours to small marks (an 8 px square, a 4 px segment).
Do draw coins with the pixel Coin icon and stars as ⭐; never show "XP".

Do give every animation a reduced-motion state: CSS durations collapse to 0.01 ms under prefers-reduced-motion, and the canvas parks its ambient motion (cars at the kerb, walkers and agents where they stand) and cuts its camera moves.
Do play a big moment in order, one thing at a time (land, rise, payoff, push-in), and time a camera flight by its distance.
Do start entrances from opacity 0.6 (the shared enter), never 0: the side panel can draw at a few frames a second, and content must show before the entrance ends.
Do keep one overlay at a time on the panel's map: one toast (the ticker steps aside), one speech bubble.
Do render in-world text with crisp() and counter-scale it by 1/zoom; keep camera zoom and sprite scales on whole numbers, and size canvas text through textPx (a mini-game's through TXT).
donts: Don't set font sizes in raw px outside the token scale: they ignore ⋯ → Text size.
Don't use Press Start 2P for running text or at sizes off its 8 px grid.
Don't fill large areas with a district colour or with amber.
Don't add a second filled button beside the primary; use a graphite or ghost button.
Don't hand-edit or regenerate the city's sprites in a UI change; they come from npm run art.
Don't start a moment's effects in the same frame, or let a celebration's zoom pop the labels on and off.
Don't give a mini-game's chrome a hex of its own: chrome is GAME_PAL; only its scene art (skies, the lake, the factory's brick, a district's colour) keeps colours of its own.
